title: A Python library for the MarketWatch stock game

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wouldn't it be fun to play a stock market game by writing code instead of clicking buttons?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Is that what this library does?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. It's a Python library from Antoine for the MarketWatch stock market game. You install it with pip, create a MarketWatch object with your username and password, and you're in.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What can you do from there?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Quite a lot. Get the current price of a stock, list the games you're in, read a game's settings and leaderboard, and check your portfolio, positions and pending orders.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Buying, selling, shorting and covering stocks in a game, plus cancelling pending orders. You can also create watchlists, add tickers to them and delete them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Like a remote control for the game.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's a good picture. One call gets a price, another places an order. The project builds on earlier community work, and it ships with tests, coverage and published documentation.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Where does it fit in his story?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The README has examples for every call.
